observation: Founder handoff in-conversation with real t3code screenshot mid-run: design substantially revised (boxy cards → dense list) AFTER initial design+critique. Signal: initial design diverged from the reference spec already cited; first /design could have hit reference closer.

Toggle decision flip-flopped: architecture-critique round 1 ruled disable-toggle WRONG (B2: no persisted state). Founder review in-conversation RESTORED toggle as real control. Later: architect corrected toggle wiring to B1 (persisted harnessDisabled + select() gate). Cost: multi-round reversal, scope addition surfaced mid-execution.

Focused architecture re-critique of the delta caught 4 real wiring seams (disabledTypes caller-supplied, builtin double-guard, discovery.disabled route-layer stamp, POST /:type/disabled validation) BEFORE build. Signal: targeted re-critique on toggle reversal paid off vs going straight to build.

Phase 4 review found 5 blockers: (1) stray eslint-disable-next-line directives in test files, (2) dead CTA button in auth zone for native_cli_login, (3) dead deprecated mappers (readinessToStatus, showsEnabledIndication, accessModeLabel), (4) undefined status tokens (--status-healthy/behind/paused/blocked/done used but not defined), (5) token-name correctness. Signal: cleanup-task completeness and code-review gate timing.

Design-critique WARNING on toggle rendered for unauthenticated backends as permanently-disabled, always-off. Initial design did not close this affordance ambiguity before hand-off to builder. Founder's real reference image clarified intent; design revised. Signal: initial variant did not interrogate reference closely enough.

Architecture-critique WARNING: runtime capabilities Fold renders 'File editing: No / MCP: No / Sub-agents: No' in production (all false) because discovery doesn't run session probe until AM3. Fixtures masked by hardcoding true. Builder had to handle gracefully ('confirmed after first run'). Signal: test fixtures obscuring production shape.

Architecture plan promised B2 (derived toggle, no persisted state) but architecture-critique ruling said 'B2 under-specified' — toggle must be non-interactive 'Enabled' OR deferred as B1 follow-up. Architect added B1 implementation anyway, expanding scope. Founder review approved B1. Signal: critique findings feed back into plan revisions, but scope expansion came mid-implementation.

Park at human-design-review gate (novel design, autonomous run) — founder reviewed rendered variant in component viewer and approved. Approval recorded in approved.md with two locked rules (real toggle, builtin not disableable). Signal: park→approve→resume flow worked as designed.

24 commits total (design → critique → founder-approval → build). Build phase ordered as tasks 1-13 but toggle decision reversed partway (task 6 implements B1 disabled-state wiring that critique said was wrong). Commits stayed fine-grained but logic flow included a mid-stream pivot.
Descriptor-driven contract (zero per-backend branching) held tight through build. No type==='codex' conditions found. Contract enforced in UI layer via mappers + backend wiring seams.

Architecture-critique SUGGESTION: promote 'zero per-backend branching' grep-for-'=== codex' gate to a real ESLint rule (design/no-restricted-syntax). Was noted as optional. Signal: static codebase properties belong in lint, not manual audits.
